fastmon-collector.disconnectHint: Disconnecting only removes the token from this shop. To revoke it on fastmon's side, remove this integration under Connected apps in the fastmon dashboard.

connect.intro: Connect this shop to a fastmon account to collect Core Web Vitals and JavaScript errors from real visitors.
connect.deviceIntro: Open fastmon and confirm this code. The shop finishes on its own once you approve.
connect.expired: The code expired before it was approved. Start again.
connect.rejected: The stored token was rejected by fastmon. It was probably revoked under Connected apps. Disconnect and connect again.
connect.unsupported: This fastmon instance does not offer the guided connection yet. Create an API token in the fastmon dashboard and paste it here instead.
connect.tokenScopes: The token needs the scopes "app:read" and "app:write", and must be bound to the organisation this shop should report to. Owner or member role - a viewer cannot create applications.
connect.missingPermission: The connected token is missing the "{permission}" permission. Add it to the token in the fastmon dashboard, or connect with an account that holds the owner or member role.

provision.intro: Choose which fastmon application this storefront reports to.
provision.name: Name
provision.autoSites: One application covers every sales channel. Each domain the storefront runs on registers itself in fastmon the first time a visitor loads a page there, so nothing has to be added by hand.
provision.pendingApproval: This fastmon organisation is still awaiting approval. fastmon reviews new accounts before they may collect data; applications can be created once it is approved, which also happens automatically on the first successful payment. The connection itself is fine - come back to this page afterwards.
provision.relink: The linked application no longer exists in fastmon, or its ids changed. The connection itself is fine - pick an application below.
provision.noneYet: This organisation has no applications yet.

summary.noSites: None yet. Each domain registers itself the first time a visitor loads a page there, so this stays empty until the storefront gets traffic.

preset.minimal: Minimal — Web Vitals and error counts only, no identifiers
preset.standard: Standard — everything that cannot contain personal data
preset.full: Full — sessions, error messages and query keys

serverTiming.title: Per-layer timings
serverTiming.lead: Where the backend time went: database, template, cache, HTTP. This is the one part of the header that needs a profiler extension on the host.
serverTiming.sourceMissing: Per-layer timings need the Tideways extension 5.23 or newer. Everything else - cache verdict and age, total time, render time, page type, server, login state - is reported regardless.

state.outdated: installed, but too old — needs 5.23 or newer

collection.needsApplication: Link a fastmon application first — the tracker and pixel ids come from it.
collection.intro: Ad blockers drop roughly a third of third-party analytics. Serving the tracker and the beacon from your own domain avoids that. The plugin does not forward those paths itself — that would put a request per pageview through PHP — so your web server has to.
collection.modeDefaultHint: Loads from fastmon.site. Works everywhere, needs no setup, and is what ad blockers recognise.
collection.modeCustomHint: One host you forward to fastmon, e.g. a measurement subdomain. First-party as long as it matches the shop's own origin.
collection.modeRelativeHint: Each storefront serves the paths from its own domain. The right choice when the shop has several — one embed covers all of them.
collection.nothingChecked: No origin could be checked, so this mode cannot be applied.
collection.secretHint: Your proxy has to send this secret in the FM-Proxy-Key header, otherwise fastmon cannot trust the visitor IP it forwards and every visitor ends up sharing the shop server's location. It is shown once — generate it again to rotate.
collection.blocked: Because of this, "{mode}" cannot be switched on — the storefronts above would load the tracker and send nothing. Set the forwarding up and check again.
collection.allReady: Every origin answers. "{mode}" can be switched on.

reason.script_status: The tracker script is not being served here: /s/ answers with HTTP {detail} instead of the fastmon bundle. Nothing forwards that path to fastmon yet.
reason.script_foreign: Something answers /s/, but it is not this application's fastmon bundle — most likely another rule catches the path first.
reason.script_unreachable: This domain could not be reached from the shop server ({detail}).
reason.collector_status: The tracker would load, but its data would go nowhere: /c/ answers with HTTP {detail} instead of reaching fastmon.
reason.collector_unreachable: The beacon path /c/ could not be reached from the shop server ({detail}).
